steps: Preheat the oven to 220C (200C fan). Press the tofu cubes between kitchen paper for 10 minutes to draw out excess moisture.
Peel and dice the sweet potato into 2cm cubes, and cut the bell pepper and broccoli into similar-sized pieces.
Toss the tofu, sweet potato, pepper and broccoli on a large baking tray with the olive oil, tamari and a pinch of garlic powder.
Spread everything in a single layer and roast for 25-30 minutes, turning once halfway, until the sweet potato is tender and the tofu edges are golden.
Divide between 4 containers once cooled for the week's meals.
Mince the salmon and salt in a food processor until smooth, or chop the fish and mix well with the salt by hand or with a hand mixer.
Add the eggs and flour and mix until the mixture has a firm consistency.
Pick and chop half of the mint. Finely chop the spring onion and finely grate the ginger.
Stir the ginger, spring onion and lime zest into the mince and season with salt and pepper.
Fry a mini fish cake in olive oil in a pan. Taste, and add salt, pepper or lime zest if necessary. Once satisfied, leave to rest for 15 minutes while you make the salad.
Cut the red cabbage and pepper into thin strips.
Dice the apple and chop the pistachios.
Mix the lemon zest, juice, honey and olive oil. Season with salt and pepper and toss with the chopped veg, fruit, pistachios and mint.
Arrange the coleslaw on a plate and top with mint, placing the fish cakes on the side with the boiled potatoes.
Preheat the grill to high. Pat the salmon dry and spread the miso paste evenly over the top.
Grill the salmon skin-side down for 8-10 minutes until the miso is caramelised and the fish flakes easily.
Meanwhile, bring a pan of water to the boil and cook the soba noodles for 4-5 minutes, then drain and rinse briefly under cold water so they don't stick.
Halve the bok choy lengthways and steam or stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until just wilted.
Toss the noodles with a splash of the cooking water, then plate with the bok choy and salmon on top.
Scatter over the sliced scallions and serve.
Preheat the oven to 220C (200C fan). Cut the potatoes into chips, toss with half the olive oil and spread on a baking tray; bake for 25-30 minutes, turning once, until golden.
Pat the fish fillet dry, brush with the remaining oil and press the breadcrumbs firmly over the top.
Place the fish on a separate tray and bake for the final 12-15 minutes of the chips' cooking time, until the crumb is golden and the fish flakes easily.
Cook the peas in boiling water for 3-4 minutes, then drain.
Serve the fish and chips with the peas and a wedge of lemon.
Preheat the oven to 200C (180C fan). Peel and chop the potatoes, then boil in salted water for 15-18 minutes until soft.
Season the fish fillet with a pinch of salt, place on a lined tray and bake for 12-15 minutes until it flakes easily.
Drain the potatoes and mash well with the butter and a little salt until smooth.
Cook the carrots in boiling water for 15-20 minutes until very soft, then drain.
Serve the fish with the mash and carrots.
Cook the jasmine rice according to the packet instructions and set aside.
Season the chicken breasts and grill or pan-fry over medium-high heat for 6-7 minutes per side until cooked through with no pink in the middle.
Steam the broccoli florets for 4-5 minutes until just tender.
Slice the chicken and divide with the rice and broccoli between 4 containers.
Drizzle each portion with teriyaki sauce and scatter over the sesame seeds before sealing for the week.

Preheat the oven to 220C (200C fan). Cut the mixed vegetables into similar-sized pieces, toss with a little olive oil and salt, spread on a tray and roast for 10 minutes, flip, then roast a further 10 minutes until tender.
Season the chicken breasts and cook in a pan or the oven until no longer pink in the middle, about 15-18 minutes, then slice.
Cook the brown rice according to the packet instructions.
Whisk the olive oil with a squeeze of lemon juice, salt and pepper to make a simple dressing.
Build each bowl with rice, chicken and roasted veg, top with sliced avocado and drizzle with the dressing.
Pull the rotisserie chicken off the bone and skin. Shred with your hands or forks. Place in a large bowl.
Add the coleslaw mix.
Chop the green onions and cucumber. Add to the bowl.
Cook the edamame and rice in the microwave according to the pack instructions. Add to the bowl.
In a small bowl, mix the tamari, hoisin sauce and chili crunch oil. Pour over the bowl of ingredients.
Mix well with two large spoons or tongs.
Cook the white rice according to the packet instructions.
Season the chicken breast with a little salt and grill or pan-fry over medium-high heat for 6-7 minutes per side until cooked through.
Peel and slice the carrots, then simmer in salted water for 15-18 minutes until very soft.
Slice the chicken and serve over the rice with the carrots, drizzled with the olive oil.
Cook the white rice according to the packet instructions.
Season and grill or pan-fry the chicken for 6-7 minutes per side until cooked through, then slice.
Warm the black beans and sweetcorn together in a small pan for 3-4 minutes.
Divide the rice between 5 containers and top each with chicken, black beans and sweetcorn.
Spoon over the salsa and guacamole and add a lime wedge to each container.
Preheat the oven to 200C (180C fan). Cut the courgette, pepper and carrot into similar-sized pieces, toss with half the olive oil and roast for 20-25 minutes until tender.
Place the salmon fillets on a separate tray, drizzle with the remaining oil and bake for the final 12-15 minutes until they flake easily.
Cook the brown rice according to the packet instructions.
Divide the rice, roasted veg and salmon between 4 containers.
Squeeze over the lemon juice before serving.
Whisk the miso, mirin and tamari together and coat the salmon fillets; leave to marinate for 10 minutes if time allows.
Thinly slice the cucumber and toss with a splash of rice vinegar and a pinch of salt; set aside to quick-pickle while you cook.
Grill or pan-fry the salmon for 3-4 minutes per side until the glaze caramelises and the fish flakes easily.
Cook the white rice according to the packet instructions and steam the greens for 3-4 minutes.
Divide the rice, greens and salmon between 4 containers and top with the pickled cucumber.
Cook the sushi rice according to the packet instructions and leave to cool slightly.
Cut the tuna into 1.5cm cubes and toss with the tamari and sesame seeds.
Dice the cucumber and slice the avocado.
Cook the edamame in boiling water for 2-3 minutes if not already cooked, then drain.
Spoon the rice into a bowl and top with the tuna, edamame, avocado and cucumber.
Arrange the California rolls on a plate.
Warm the miso soup according to the pack instructions.
Steam or microwave the edamame for 2-3 minutes until hot, then drain.
Serve the rolls with the miso soup, edamame and a small dish of tamari for dipping.
